newsitem.title: JAPAN: Omron sees April-July group profit above forecast.
newsitem.headline: Omron sees April-July group profit above forecast.

text.p: Omron Corp President Yoshio Tateishi said on Friday that the company expects its April-July group profit to significantly surpass the forecast it issued earlier this year.
Tateishi also said it was possible that Omron's group profit forecast for the year to March 31, 1998 would be revised upward.
"Our group sales in the April-July period were up about 10 percent from a year earlier because of robust sales of control devices, especially in the overseas markets," Tateishi said.
He also said that group profitability had improved as a result of cost-cutting measures.
He said sales in the domestic market in the April-July period increased about seven to eight percent from a year ago amid rising demand from small and medium-sized firms for control components.
Overseas sales rose around 15 percent year-on-year, mainly due to strong sales of information- and communications-related equipment, he said.
"It is possible that our forecast for group profits for the full year will be revised," said Tateishi.
In May, Omron forecast group sales of 645 billion yen for the 1997/98 business year, up nine percent from the previous year, while group net profit was expected to rise 27 percent to 20 billion yen.
